sections.h2: What the Mason County Register of Deeds keeps
sections.html:
Everything that moves title to land in the county, or burdens it, ends up on file here. The register is an elected officer on a four-year term, and MCL 565.551 obliges the office to give the public reasonable facilities to examine and copy the records.

The register also leads the county plat board, a three-seat panel that reviews proposed subdivisions before they reach the state.

The counter keeps three separate schedules, all skipping legal holidays:

  • General business, 9 to 5
  • Accepting documents for the record, 9 to 4:30
  • Passport applications, 9 to 3

Ask the office for its street address and direct phone line before you send a package.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Mason County
sections.html:
Ludington is the county seat and the biggest city. Of the county's 1,242 square miles, only 495 are land, and much of the rest lies under Lake Michigan. M-116 follows the lakeshore to Ludington State Park, which draws seasonal visitors.

The county had an estimated 29,040 residents for 2025, almost unchanged since 2020. It is an older, owner-heavy market:

  • Homeowners report a typical value of $219,600
  • 78.3 percent of homes are lived in by owners
  • Rent for a typical unit comes to $896
  • 28.8 percent of residents are 65 or older

Filing one deed, mortgage or lis pendens costs $30.00. When a single paper discharges or assigns several instruments, each extra one costs $3.00. Ordinary copies are $1.00 per page, plats are $2.00, and a certification stamp is $5.00.

If staff run a name search for you, the price is 50 cents for every year covered, never less than $5.00, and a state or federal tax lien certificate search costs $3.00 a name. Fee schedules change, so ring the office to verify a figure before you cut the check.

Images and indexes reach back to June 23, 1840 and are online. Heavy users can buy a prepaid subscription, and occasional users can pay by card per search. The index is a working tool that may contain mistakes and is not a certified search.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Mason County sale
sections.html:
The county's table stacks $3.75 of state tax and $0.55 of county tax on each $500 of price, which makes $4.30 per slice. The grantor owes it on any deed given for $100 or more.

Separate exemption pages cover the county share and the state share. If one applies, say so on the deed itself. Foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, and land contracts that have not yet passed title are on the exempt list.

sections.h2: What a deed must show to be accepted
sections.html:
The register publishes the full text of MCL 565.201 as its standard. The short version for a modern deed: legible names under the signatures, the notary's name printed nearby, grantee addresses, and a preparer's name and business address.

Format rules run alongside those. Leave a clear strip about 2 1/2 inches deep at the top of the first sheet, print in 10 point or larger, and stay between letter and legal size. A single recordable event belongs on the first line. A translation must accompany foreign-language text, and most of a Social Security number has to be blanked.

Once the register accepts and records a deed, the law treats it as conforming. A compliant deed cannot be refused because of what it says, so closing agents proof the document before it is presented.

The county treasurer signs off on deeds ahead of recording, confirming nothing is delinquent for the five years before the instrument date, and hands out tax abstracts on request. Under MCL 211.135 that certificate goes with warranty deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments.

Counter hours are weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax line is 231 843-8411. Each March 1 the township and city rolls come to the county in a step called settlement, and unpaid real property tax becomes the treasurer's to collect. Village taxes run on a different timetable.

Since 2004 Mason County has run its own tax foreclosures, so the treasurer's staff run title searches, mail notices and sell tax-delinquent parcels instead of the state. The county also audits principal residence exemptions, so any exemption claimed in error is pursued from the same office.

If you owe back taxes when you sell, the usual route is to have the closing agent pay the balance from your proceeds, which clears the way for the certificate.

Equalization handles these. It keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5 and answers at 231-845-6288. The department issues addresses for every unit except Ludington and Scottville, splits and combines tax parcels, takes mailing address updates and supplies aerial and tax maps. It also links the county parcel GIS layer, the apportionment report and the yearly equalization report.

Splits come up when a buyer wants only part of a lot or a lakeside piece is being divided. The register records the new deed, and equalization then revises the parcel records.

Owners can also sign up free for the register's Property Fraud Alert.

sections.h2: What to bring when you record
sections.html:
Bring the signed original deed, the fee, and the treasurer's certificate if the deed carries warranties. Check that the preparer's name and business address, the grantee's address and the notary details are all on the page. If a transfer tax exemption applies, make sure the deed says so.

Arrive before 4:30 on a weekday, since recording stops half an hour before the front office closes. A deed handed in late can slide to the next business day.

After recording, the register's index and images update online, and equalization revises the parcel records. Ask the closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed for your files. If you sold for cash and the buyer's agent handled the filing, confirm with the register's office that the deed was indexed under the right parcel and names.

If the sale involves a land contract that has not yet passed title, ask the closing agent whether the transfer tax exemption applies and how it must be worded on the paper that gets recorded.

faqs.q: What is the Mason County deed filing price?
faqs.a: It is $30.00 for each document, with $3.00 more for every additional instrument it releases. Copies are $1.00 a page and certification is $5.00.

faqs.q: What time does Mason County stop taking deeds for the record?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, half an hour before the front office closes at 5. A deed handed in late can slide to the next business day.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Mason County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays, unless the deed states an exemption. The combined rate is $4.30 for each $500 of price, and the county's table shows the total at each price level.

faqs.q: Does a Mason County warranty deed need anything from the treasurer?
faqs.a: Yes. The county treasurer must certify that no taxes are delinquent for the previous five years before the register records it. A quitclaim without warranty language is excused under MCL 211.135.

faqs.q: How far back do Mason County online land records go?
faqs.a: Images and indexes are online from June 23, 1840 to the present. The index is a working index, so check any key detail against the recorded document.
